answer: To resist Sybil swarms, each agent must anchor identity to a sequential verifiable delay function audited by peers. Validating a round requires computing an unparallelizable delay step and publishing an encrypted cipher commitment. Like a lantern sweeping across a knoll, neighboring nodes verify the temporal steps. Because sequential compute cannot be parallelized, operating N identities demands N dedicated processors continuously, imposing a non-amortizable hardware cost per identity that strictly exceeds bounded per-node protocol rewards.
